definition: A modular neural network is an artificial neural network characterized by a series of independent neural networks moderated by some intermediary, such as a cohomological structure of Cohomology Theory.
details: Each independent neural network serves as a module and operates on separate inputs to accomplish some subtask of the task the network hopes to perform. The intermediary takes the outputs of each module and processes them to produce the output of the network as a whole. The intermediary only accepts the modules' outputs—it does not respond to, nor otherwise signal, the modules. As well, the modules do not interact with each other.

explainer.lead: A modular neural network splits work across independent networks, each handling a subtask, with an intermediary combining their outputs. This isolates computation so no module needs to see or coordinate with the others.

tiers.eli5: Like separate specialists each solving their own part of a puzzle while a coordinator assembles their answers into the final result.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers give each module its own separate inputs and let only the intermediary process their outputs. A pitfall: the intermediary only accepts module outputs and cannot signal back, and modules cannot interact, so coordination must come entirely from the intermediary's combination step.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the network is a set of independent neural networks operating on separate inputs for subtasks, moderated by an intermediary (such as a cohomological structure of Cohomology Theory) that takes only their outputs to produce the overall output; no signalling to modules occurs.

explainer.example: Several independent networks each process a distinct portion of the input; the intermediary collects their outputs and produces the network's single final output.
